result.rationale: The specified passenger-car sense overlaps. Both words have broader meanings, but those do not change the intended referent. DBP labels car-sense mobil as Indonesian and uses kereta in Malaysian car terminology; contemporary Malaysian reporting and government usage also use kereta. Indonesian transport usage consistently uses mobil and distinguishes it from kereta api. The checked evidence does not establish kereta as an ordinary Indonesian word for a car or mobil as an ordinary Malaysian one. The audit repeats some sources across claim IDs and provides no conversational frequency study, so its everyday-preference claim is qualitative. Those limits do not leave a material objection to different-common-word.
